long_biography.plain_text:
Ford grew up in Te Puke, where his father managed farms assembled by three generations of the family. He worked in Auckland wool stores, studied wool classing and travelled to Britain for further industry training before settling in Australia as a junior wool buyer. In 1981, he and Dianne formed Ford Land, which developed a portfolio across metropolitan Sydney.

The company combines property investment, ownership, leasing, refurbishment and in-house management, concentrating on industrial estates, warehouses, showrooms and commercial offices. Ford also chairs Ford Land Holdings, the family vehicle that owns The Sandhills at Te Tumu. The New Zealand holding began with land acquired by his grandfather and was expanded by successive generations, while Ford’s Australian property activity created a separate urban commercial platform.
